Thanks, Tessa / Alicia — I reviewed the attachment quickly and sketched out initial engineering validation items below. Short answers first, then a proposed sandbox checklist.

Quick guidance:
- VPC / On-prem: For VPC private deployments we recommend a service-to-service peering model with strict egress rules. If they plan on running Redwood Private on-prem, our reference uses a thin control plane + local execution nodes. We'll need their network diagrams to confirm ports (gRPC 8000, metrics 9000) and NAT behavior.
- Batching & KV cache: Their session routing that fans out across agents could cause fragmented KV caches. Recommend session affinity for same-client requests (sticky routing) and a prefix cache layer for repeated system prompts. We can provide a caching shim to reduce cold-start tokens.
- Models / quantization: For 8k token workflows we typically recommend a q4_0 or q5_x profile for throughput on T4/A10-like hardware in Dedicated, and full fp16 for low-latency Hosted (if the customer tolerates the cost). Provide tradeoffs in the sandbox report.
- Fallbacks: Configure model-family fallbacks: primary fp16 8k -> q4_0 8k -> small 4k quantized. Also implement a token-cutoff policy for streaming long outputs to avoid tail latency.

Proposed sandbox checklist (what we'll run on our side):
1) Connectivity: VPC peering test + TLS mutual auth handshake
2) End-to-end sample flow: 10 concurrent sessions, 50 req/s sustained, capture per-token latency
3) KV-cache behavior: warm vs cold session comparison, measure token reductions
4) Model variant regression: same prompt across fp16/q4 to surface hallucination/quality delta
5) Failure injection: drop 10% of requests and validate fallbacks + tracing

Attachments: redwood-integration-checklist.xlsx (I'll upload the checklist and test harness notes).

Alicia — can you share a candidate sample dataset (anonymized) and one representative 8k session trace? That will help us calibrate sequence lengths and expected cache hit rates.

I'll block time on Tue Apr 6 10:30 PT for the deep-dive unless you prefer another slot.

—Jonas

We can provide full network diagrams and our Terraform module for peering. We use mTLS for service auth and will share our cert rotation docs.

Agree — we can pin sessions to a node group for a TTL of 6 hours. We will also share a sample trace (attached) and a small anonymized dataset of 1,200 session transcripts.

We ran an internal perf run on q4_0 and saw ~2.2x throughput improvement vs fp16 on A10 for large batches; quality delta was small for most prompts but we will provide a list of prompts that are sensitive.
